```{r setup}
library(bioRtools)
library(ggplot2)
```

This workflow uses the public `GlobalPatterns` dataset distributed with the
Bioconductor package `mia` (Caporaso et al., 2011; DOI
10.1073/pnas.1000080107).

```{r data, eval = requireNamespace("mia", quietly = TRUE)}
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "mia")

X <- t(as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(GlobalPatterns)))
meta <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(GlobalPatterns))
rownames(X) <- meta$X.SampleID
meta$sample <- meta$X.SampleID
rownames(meta) <- meta$X.SampleID
taxo <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(GlobalPatterns))

dim(X)
head(meta[, c("sample", "SampleType")])
```

## Alpha diversity

```{r alpha, eval = requireNamespace("mia", quietly = TRUE)}
alpha <- calc_alpha_diversity(
  X,
  sample = meta,
  index = c("shannon", "observed", "chao1"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

head(alpha)
```

## Bray-Curtis PCoA and PERMANOVA

```{r ordination, eval = requireNamespace("mia", quietly = TRUE)}
ordination <- pcoa_analysis(X, sample = meta, color = "SampleType")
ordination$plots$score_plot

set.seed(1)
permanova <- permanova_test(
  X ~ SampleType,
  sample = meta,
  permutations = 999
)
permanova$tables$permanova
```

## Taxonomic composition

```{r composition, eval = requireNamespace("mia", quietly = TRUE)}
composition <- top_tax_n(
  data = X,
  sample = meta,
  taxo = taxo,
  which = "Phylum",
  group_col = "SampleType",
  plot_by = "group",
  plot_type = "stacked_bar",
  ref = "Feces",
  verbose = FALSE
)

composition$plot_abundance
```

The result objects retain their native ordination or model content, while the
`tables` and `plots` components follow the shared `bioRtools_fit` contract.
